EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw a significant escalation in the US-Iran conflict, with the US continuing nightly airstrikes on Iranian military targets and Iran retaliating against US bases in the region, while President Trump issued stark new threats concerning the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, the US approved a civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, drawing sharp criticism from Israel and raising proliferation concerns.

IRAN
The US military completed its eleventh consecutive night of strikes against Iran, targeting military operations centers, naval capabilities, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities, and logistics infrastructure to weaken Iran's ability to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Health Ministry reports 53 people killed and 592 injured in US airstrikes across the country since June 27. Iranian state media and military sources reported several US strikes across Iran, including Sirik, Bushehr, Tabriz, Mahshahr, Behbahan, Bandar Abbas, Chadar, Qeshm, Kangavar, Baneh, and multiple locations around Tehran (Parchin, Khajir). Satellite imagery reportedly showed the destruction of an aircraft hangar at King Faisal Air Base in Jordan, and an AN/FPS-117 early-warning radar system at Ahmed Al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait, attributed to Iranian retaliatory strikes. Iran's Armed Forces spokesman, Brigadier General Shekarchi, stated that Iran's strategic missile production continues without halt, moving directly from production to operational use, and asserted that "five decades of US investments in its bases in West Asia were destroyed." He also claimed a massive US data center in the UAE, built over 20 years with European and Zionist regime investment, was destroyed by Iran. Iran executed Mehdi Khanaki, accused of involvement in January protests and acting "in favor of Israel and the US." The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, denied any nuclear activity at Kolang Kouh (Pickaxe Mountain) near Natanz, calling US focus on it "a fabricated pretext for aggression, destruction, and sabotage." A military source warned that if the US targets any Iranian bridge or power plant, Iran will retaliate against US-linked regional infrastructure, including energy facilities. The IRGC has warned of a "regret-inducing operation" that would lead to "public mourning" in the US if strikes continue. Iran views attacks on its nuclear and vital sites as an expansion of war.

ISRAEL
The Israeli military released intelligence details on 12 individuals previously presented as Palestinian soccer players, identifying them as Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) terrorists, some involved in the October 7 invasion. Among those named are Mohammed Barakat (PIJ, Oct 7 invader), Mahmoud Kamal Mohammed Ali Al-Rifi (Hamas aerial company commander), Mohammed Mansour (Hamas Nuseirat Battalion deputy commander, Oct 7 invader), and Mohammed Sami Mohammed Khattab (FIFA international referee, PIJ member). The IDF reported killing several armed PIJ and other gunmen in the southern Gaza Strip yesterday, who were moving weapons for attacks against IDF troops. Explosions were heard in Eilat after Iranian ballistic missiles targeted the nearby Jordanian city of Aqaba, with no reported impacts in Israeli territory. Prime Minister Netanyahu reiterated his commitment to deepening unity and forming a broad national government. The government informed the Supreme Court that legislation for a 7 October inquiry would be completed after elections, prompting criticism from the "October Council." Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman vehemently criticized the US-Saudi civilian nuclear deal, warning of a regional nuclear arms race and a loss of Israeli influence. The security cabinet is scheduled to convene on Sunday evening in response to escalating tensions. Discussions are ongoing between the White House and the Israeli PM's office regarding a potential meeting between President Trump and PM Netanyahu next week. Families of hostages killed by friendly fire (Alon Shamriz, Yotam Haim, Samer al-Talalka) petitioned the Supreme Court for full military investigations and information on rules of engagement. The US Embassy in Israel issued a "level 2: exercise increased caution" alert for US citizens, noting a rise in violence related to organized crime in Tel Aviv, Jaffa, and Herzliya. An Israeli military exercise is planned for tomorrow morning in the Northern Western Negev, with no security incident anticipated.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF confirmed the killing of 12 Palestinian "soccer players" in the Gaza Strip, stating they were members of Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, some of whom participated in the October 7 attacks. In the southern Gaza Strip, the IDF carried out airstrikes against multiple armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives and other gunmen spotted transferring weapons into a vehicle. Two individuals from Shuafat refugee camp were arrested for allegedly planning an immediate attack in Jerusalem. Palestinian leader Khalil al-Hayya, the new head of Hamas's political bureau, called on friendly nations to pressure Israel to implement agreements and asserted the right of the Palestinian people to liberation and statehood.

LEBANON
The Golani Brigade has been operating in southern Lebanon for four months, reportedly crossing the Litani and Saluki rivers, capturing historical ridges, and conducting operations. Lebanese reports indicated an Israeli strike in the town of Kounine in southern Lebanon. The IDF's Arabic spokesperson claimed Hezbollah planted an IED that exploded near two Red Cross ambulances in Mifdon, southern Lebanon, injuring several crew members. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that Hezbollah's disarmament would be possible only if there is an end to occupation and full, exclusive control by the army, as well as a government-led reconstruction program. Official sources reported that new talks between Israel and Lebanon are expected to be held in Italy on August 4.

SYRIA & IRAQ
An explosion was reported in Erbil Governorate in northern Iraq. Iraqi Prime Minister Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Iran tomorrow, Thursday. Iraqi officials announced the appointment of Lieutenant General Muhammad Qassem Al-Fahad as the new commander of the Iraqi Federal Police and Lieutenant General Jaafar Abdul Amir Hussein as acting commander of the Special Division. Reports mentioned failed attempts to intercept an Iranian drone in Syria heading towards a US base. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio encouraged Syria to focus on its internal problems.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued a National Early Warning alert for Dammam, advising residents to follow emergency safety steps, and later announced the "potential danger has passed." Reports from Saudi Arabia described explosions near King Fahd Airport and in Al Khobar, with some attributing a missile attack to targeting the American base in Dammam. Bahrain's Defense Force reported intercepting multiple Iranian aerial attacks, confirming a "systematic hostile approach" targeting civilians and hearing sirens and explosions. Kuwait's General Staff stated its air defenses were countering hostile drone attacks due to "Iran's brazen aggression," with explosions heard resulting from interceptions. CGTN reported satellite images showed Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar completely empty, with US aircraft, including refueling tankers and military transports, evacuated. The EU Naval Force advised commercial vessels linked to the US, Israel, or Saudi Arabia to avoid transiting the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, citing risks of UAV and anti-ship missile attacks. Four oil tankers were reported to have changed their course in the Red Sea. Goldman Sachs analysts warned oil could reach $120 a barrel unless exports through the Strait of Hormuz restart, while Brent crude breached $95 a barrel, a six-week high. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman condemned Iranian attacks on Kuwaiti territory in a call with Kuwaiti Amir Sheikh Meshal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah, affirming full solidarity. A US official quoted by CNBC stated Houthis have completed preparations to attack shipping in the Red Sea's southern access point, deploying missiles and drones near Bab el-Mandeb.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  President Trump explicitly threatened that "any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz... the United States will bomb and destroy one bridge or power plant," including those in or near Tehran.
2.  The US approved a civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia, potentially allowing the kingdom to enrich uranium on its soil, reportedly without a prior condition of normalization with Israel.
3.  Iran reported 53 people killed and 592 injured in US airstrikes across the country since June 27, and claimed responsibility for retaliatory strikes on US bases in Jordan (Al-Faysal, Prince Hassan), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa, Ahmed Al-Jaber), destroying F-15 preparation hangars, MQ-9 drones, and heavy helicopters.
4.  EASA issued a severe warning to airlines, recommending avoidance of Jordanian airspace until August 31, 2026, due to Iranian attacks and escalating military tensions.
5.  Bahrain and Saudi Arabia (Dammam) reported sirens, alerts, and interceptions of Iranian aerial attacks, indicating active regional engagement in the conflict.
6.  The IDF released intelligence identifying 12 individuals previously portrayed as Palestinian soccer players as Hamas and PIJ terrorists, some involved in the October 7 invasion.
7.  The US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stated the cost of the war with Iran has reached $37.5 billion and requested additional billions from Congress to continue military operations.
8.  Talks between Israel and Lebanon are scheduled to take place in Italy on August 4, aiming to address cross-border issues amid ongoing tensions.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following President Trump's explicit threat to target Iranian civilian infrastructure, including bridges and power plants in Tehran, in response to any Iranian aggression in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's reciprocal threats to target US-linked regional infrastructure, coupled with its claims of destroying US military assets, signify a direct and rapidly expanding military confrontation. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran asserts full control and the Houthis are threatening Saudi-bound shipping, and US military bases in the Gulf (Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait), which Iran claims to have successfully targeted. The US approval of a Saudi civilian nuclear program, without requiring normalization with Israel, could catalyze a regional nuclear arms race, further destabilizing the Middle East and potentially increasing proliferation risks. The continued US airstrikes on Iran (11th consecutive night) and Iran's stated commitment to inflicting "public mourning" on the US if attacks persist indicate a low probability of de-escalation in the immediate future. The involvement of Bulgaria in hosting US refueling aircraft, despite Iranian warnings of complicity in war crimes, expands the geographical scope of potential military posture changes.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump maintained a hardline stance, reiterating that Iran will "pay a heavy price" and "are being destroyed," while also claiming "Americans are not against the war." He approved a civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia allowing uranium enrichment. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth revealed the war on Iran has cost $37.5 billion and requested tens of billions more from Congress, facing intense questioning from senators. Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused Iran of fueling instability and not being serious about negotiations, despite direct and indirect Iranian attempts to negotiate. The US Embassy in Israel issued a security alert for citizens regarding organized crime, and in Jordan, warned citizens of insecurity outside. CENTCOM confirmed the 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, stating targets included military operations, naval capabilities, drone facilities, and logistics.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia issued emergency alerts in Dammam and confirmed the passing of a "potential danger," while also reporting explosions near King Fahd Airport and in Al Khobar. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman condemned Iranian attacks on Kuwait and affirmed solidarity. Bahrain's Defense Force confirmed interceptions of Iranian aerial attacks and a "systematic hostile approach." Kuwait's General Staff stated its air defenses were countering Iranian drone attacks.
**EU Members:** The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued a severe warning, recommending airlines avoid Jordanian airspace until August 31, 2026. Bulgaria's parliament approved the temporary stationing of up to 8 US tanker aircraft and 250 personnel at Bezmer air base from July 24 to October 1, despite Iran's warning of complicity in "aggression and war crimes." Italy is set to host new talks between Israel and Lebanon on August 4.
**Russia:** Russia's Foreign Minister denied providing weapons to Tehran in the conflict with the US and China. Mikhail Ulyanov, Russia's Permanent Representative in Vienna, stated Iran is serious about negotiations but will not accept dictates or ultimatums.
**China:** China's Foreign Minister called on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to "respect Beijing's core interests" and "address its legitimate concerns." Ambassador Zong Peiwu stated China is willing to play a constructive role in restoring peace and tranquility to the Middle East.
**Turkey:** A Hebrew media report claimed senior Israeli officials alleged Turkey threatened to provide air support to Iran if Kurdish forces enter Iranian territory as part of an Israeli ground plan.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are significant contradictions and unverified claims, particularly regarding the scale and impact of strikes. Iranian state media and military sources claim extensive destruction of US military assets and infrastructure (e.g., eight MQ-9 drones, heavy helicopters, US data center in UAE, F-15 preparation hangars), while US CENTCOM reports only focus on weakening Iranian capabilities without detailing US losses. Citizen reports from Iran (via @mamlekate and @VahidOnline) describe widespread explosions and air defense activity across many cities, often attributing them to US strikes, though official Iranian statements often refer to them as "projectiles" or "hostile drones." The claim by @omid_dana that "all of the IRGC's water heaters were intercepted by Saudi Arabia and not even one hit" is likely propaganda or sarcasm, lacking verifiable detail. The report by @omid_dana about 24,000 US and Japanese marines being deployed to the Middle East for a "definite ground attack" is unconfirmed and needs further verification. The claim by the Iranian military source that "Iran will target several infrastructures and energy facilities in the region where America has interests" if Iranian infrastructure is hit is a threat, not a factual report of an action taken. The US Embassy warning to citizens in Israel regarding organized crime is noteworthy as it highlights internal security concerns separate from the regional conflict. There is a reporting gap regarding independent confirmation of casualties and damage figures from US strikes in Iran, as well as the effectiveness of Iranian retaliatory strikes beyond Iranian and pro-Iranian media claims.
